verses.text: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and his disciples.
He said, “The teachers of the Law and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.”
“So do what they tell you from the Law, but don’t copy how they act. They talk, but they don’t live it.”
“They pile heavy loads on people’s shoulders—loads that are hard to carry—but won’t lift a finger to help.”
“Everything they do is for show. They make their Scripture boxes extra wide and the tassels on their clothes extra long.”
“They love the best seats at banquets and the front-row seats in synagogues,”
“the big greetings in the marketplaces, and being called ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by everyone.”
“But you shouldn’t be called ‘Rabbi.’ You have one teacher, the Christ, and you’re all siblings.”
“Don’t call anyone on earth your father. You have one Father, and he’s in heaven.”
“Don’t let people call you masters either. You have one master, the Christ.”
“The greatest among you must serve everyone else.”
“Whoever lifts themselves up will be brought low; whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up.”
“How terrible for you, teachers of the Law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You exploit widows’ homes, then cover it up with long prayers. Your judgment will be worse.”
“How terrible for you, teachers of the Law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut Heaven’s Kingdom in people’s faces. You won’t go in, and you block those who are trying to enter.”
“How terrible for you, teachers of the Law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You travel land and sea to win one convert. Then you make them twice as much a child of Gehenna as you are.”
“How terrible for you, blind guides! You say, ‘Swearing by the temple means nothing, but swearing by its gold makes you bound to your oath.’”
“Blind fools! Which is greater—the gold, or the temple that makes the gold sacred?”
“You also say, ‘Swearing by the altar means nothing, but swearing by the gift on it makes you bound.’”
“Blind fools! Which is greater—the gift, or the altar that makes the gift sacred?”
“Whoever swears by the altar swears by it and everything on it.”
“Whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who lives in it.”
“Whoever swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One sitting on it.”

“How terrible for you, teachers of the Law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You tithe mint, dill, and cumin, but skip the weightier parts of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should’ve practiced those without neglecting the others.”
“Blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.”
“How terrible for you, teachers of the Law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of your cup and plate, but inside they’re full of extortion and unrighteousness.”
“Blind Pharisee! Clean the inside of the cup first, so the outside can be clean too.”
“How terrible for you, teachers of the Law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You’re like whitewashed tombs: beautiful on the outside, but inside full of dead bones and uncleanness.”
“In the same way, you look righteous to people on the outside, but inside you’re full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.”
“How terrible for you, teachers of the Law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the graves of righteous people,”
“then say, ‘If we’d lived in our ancestors’ days, we wouldn’t have joined them in killing the prophets.’”
“So you’re testifying against yourselves: you’re the children of those who killed the prophets.”
“Go ahead, then—finish what your ancestors started.”
“You snakes! You brood of vipers! How are you going to escape Gehenna’s judgment?”
“So listen: I’m sending you prophets, wise people, and teachers. You’ll kill and crucify some, whip others in your synagogues, and chase them from town to town,”
“so the blame for all the righteous blood shed on earth will land on you—from righteous Abel’s blood to Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.”
“I’m telling you the truth: all this will come down on this generation.”
“Jerusalem, Jerusalem—you kill the prophets and stone the people sent to you! How many times I wanted to gather your children like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you wouldn’t let me.”
“Look, your house is being left empty.”
“I’m telling you, you won’t see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name!’”
